topic.title: Accessibility Support in Web Author
topic.shortdesc: Overview of accessibility support and assistive technology features in .

body.p: is designed to be usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. It is developed and improved to comply with the U.S. Government Section 508 accessibility standards, the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), and the Harmonised European Standard Accessibility requirements for ICT products and services.
The goal is to ensure that is accessible and functional for all users, including those who use assistive technologies such as screen readers.

Some of the accessibility features in include:
The ability to work with Web Author using the keyboard without using a mouse.
The various UI components and areas within the application (such as dialog boxes and views) are accessible to screen readers. has been tested with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver.
Features (such as change tracking) are interpreted by screen readers.
An Enable accessibility optimization option optimizes the editor for accessibility and provides more information for screen readers.
Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
Many common keyboard shortcuts are available, and additional shortcuts are provided (for example, on Windows, Ctrl+F2 instructs the screen reader to provide more information about an element).
You can navigate through the various UI components by using keyboard commands (for example, on Windows, Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter, space bar, and Ctrl+F6/Shift+Ctrl+F6 navigate through the main regions of the UI).
Color contrast is adjusted to comply with the required standards.
A spell check dialog box (accessed via a toolbar button or F7) lets you cycle through misspelled words and replace them with the correct ones.The installation kit does not include this feature by default, but you can enable it by installing a plugin available on GitHub.
